verdict.rationale: Clerk documents a substantial programmatic surface: a published OpenAPI spec, a Backend API that personal access tokens can call, MCP account tools for creating apps, managing users and setting up production instances, and CLI commands for deployment configuration. It also keeps moving features to the API, such as making the logs endpoint public. Nothing in the evidence claims or shows full parity between the Dashboard/UI and the API, so this is partial. missing for 10: an explicit API-parity commitment, evidence that all Dashboard settings and workspace/team management are API-accessible, independent hands-on confirmation of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Access tokens: Create personal access tokens for the Clerk Backend API.
Account tools: Create and configure applications, manage users, and set up production instances in your Clerk workspace.
APIs and prebuilt UIs for sign-up, sign-in, and user profile
The GET /v1/logs endpoint is now public, so you can look up Application Logs events from your own code or an AI agent.
A new Backend API endpoint merges a duplicate user into another and deletes the duplicate.
